sentences.text: America's most hated group chat writes every law.
Who's in it? Why does nothing get sent? Where's the president?
The House: 435, one per district, every two years.
The Senate: two per state, for six years.
But here's the weird part: Wyoming gets as many senators as California!
Every law, every tax, every dollar: through this chat.
The president? Not even in the chat.
Both chats pass the same text. He signs... or vetoes.
Now it gets strange: ignore a bill for ten days, and it's law anyway!
No deal on money? Shutdown. Last year: 43 days.
On November 3, Democrats took both chats.
Now every law needs both parties. Expect a lot of 'left on read'.
Send this to the friend who never replies.
And those typing dots? Senators talking. The record: 25 hours. Ending it takes 60 votes.
So, should the Senate scrap the sixty-vote rule?
